solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Drink oddly seen in clean house

indicators.note: in places the picked letters inside the cleaning word

parts.note: to char is to clean someone's house for pay

indicators.note: oddly asks for the letters in odd positions of the word seen

explanation.surface: Someone sneaks a drink while cleaning a house and is spotted doing it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' takes S and E (letters 1 and 3) from 'seen', and 'in' puts them inside CHAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaser is a drink taken straight after another, such as beer after a shot of spirits.

clue.text: Mum's after a computer game

indicators.note: after says the mother word comes behind the computer's name

parts.note: HAL is the computer in the film 2001: A Space Odyssey
mum is, for the surface; MA is a word for mum

explanation.surface: A child says Mum is chasing a computer game.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's in 'Mum's' is read as 'is', so the clue says the mother comes after the computer.
explanation.definitionFit: Halma is a board game in which players jump pieces across a square board, the forerunner of Chinese chequers.

clue.text: Some pupils, by splitting from this, failed

indicators.note: splitting says the multiplication sign breaks the jumbled letters apart
failed suggests the words from this have gone wrong and must be rearranged

parts.note: X means by, as in measurements such as three by four

explanation.surface: Pupils drop out of their year group and then fail their exams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'failed' turns FROM THIS into SITHFORM, and X ('by') goes inside, 'splitting' it after SI.
explanation.definitionFit: In British schools the sixth form is the final two years' group of older pupils, so it is a body of some pupils.

clue.text: Rule for one that ruler's upset about

indicators.note: about says the upturned title wraps around the example abbreviation
upset in a down clue turns the ruler's title upside down, reading it backwards

parts.note: an emir is a Muslim ruler; the 's is ruler is, for the surface
for one means for example, abbreviated EG

explanation.surface: A rule that troubles the ruler who must enforce it.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'upset' means turned upside down, so the ruler's title reads from the bottom up.
explanation.definitionFit: A regime is a government or system of control, so it is a period of rule.

clue.text: Just manage to get junk article off eBay?

parts.note: scrap means junk

indicators.note: off says the article is removed from the website name

parts.note: the auction website, its letters taken as written
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Trying to sell junk on eBay to earn enough to get by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' removes A from EBAY, leaving EBY.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrape by is an idiom for surviving with barely enough money, just managing.

clue.text: Rivers e.g. hold water — guide across channels?

parts.note: an argument that holds water stands up

indicators.note: across says the steering word stretches over the channels word

parts.note: to con a ship is to steer or guide it
the media are channels of communication

explanation.surface: Rivers hold water, and someone guides boats along canal channels.
explanation.walkthrough: Rivers is Joan Rivers, the American comic, not waterways; 'hold water' is the idiom for an argument being sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Joan Rivers was a famous comic who performed solo routines on stage, an example of that kind of performer.

clue.text: Tenant's payment to landlord out of hand?

indicators.note: out of here says the payment is on the outside of the hand word

parts.note: rent is what a tenant pays a landlord
a hand is a side, as in on the left hand

explanation.surface: A tenant's rent payment to the landlord has spiralled out of control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of hand' looks like 'uncontrolled', but 'out of' puts RENT outside SIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: A resident lives in a place, as a tenant does in a rented home.

clue.text: Look for an audience to wind up

indicators.note: for an audience means as heard by listeners, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: to peek is to take a quick look

explanation.surface: A performer looks for spectators to tease.
explanation.definitionFit: To pique someone is to irritate or annoy them, the same as winding them up in British slang.

clue.text: Not seeing death? That's new over in heaven

indicators.note: in places them inside the heavenly word

parts.note: bliss means heaven, perfect happiness

indicators.note: over says the death word and the new letter are read backwards

parts.note: death is the end

explanation.surface: A meditation on death: losing sight on earth but gaining new vision in heaven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' reads the death word plus the new letter backwards, giving NDNE.
explanation.definitionFit: Blindness is the state of lacking sight, of not seeing.

clue.text: A plastic pig is outside the law, miss

indicators.note: is outside says the animal word wraps around the Latin law

parts.note: lex is Latin for law
a miss is a girl or lass

explanation.surface: A plastic pig sits out of the law's reach, miss.
explanation.walkthrough: Lex, Latin for law, is a common crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Plexiglas is a trade name for a clear acrylic sheet, a type of plastic.

clue.text: Stop wasting time with a variable pump

indicators.note: wasting suggests the time letter is lost from the stopping word

parts.note: to quit is to stop
Z is a letter used in algebra as an unknown or variable

explanation.surface: Stop dawdling with that adjustable pump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wasting' removes T from QUIT, leaving QUI.
explanation.definitionFit: To pump someone is to question them persistently for information, which is what a quiz does.

clue.text: Got fine reception with old copper

parts.note: F is the pencil abbreviation for fine
an at-home is a reception held in one's house
D was the abbreviation for the old British penny, a copper coin

explanation.surface: Someone got a good welcome alongside a veteran police officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' wants to be a policeman; it is the old penny, D, from pre-1971 British money.
explanation.definitionFit: Got in the sense of understood: to fathom something is to get to the bottom of it.

clue.text: Old men gathering on subject of hairstyle

definitions.note: a plural word used as the name of one style

indicators.note: gathering says the fathers word collects the subject word inside it

parts.note: old man is slang for father, so old men are dads
re means on the subject of

explanation.surface: Elderly men gather to discuss a hairstyle.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreads is short for dreadlocks, a style of long matted ropes of hair.

clue.text: The decision of corrupt officials, in part

indicators.note: in part says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A decision made by crooked officials.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in part' takes the letters spanning 'corrupt officials'.
explanation.definitionFit: 'It's up to you' means it is your choice, so the phrase stands for whose decision it is.

clue.text: Square peg out to keep up, too

indicators.note: to keep says the dying word holds the reversed word inside

parts.note: to peg out is slang for to die or perish

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the word too reads backwards

parts.note: taken as the word itself

explanation.surface: A square peg drops out to keep up with everyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' reverses, giving OOT. Pooter is the fussy clerk in the comic novel The Diary of a Nobody.
explanation.definitionFit: Pooterish describes a self-important, petty, conventional manner, like Charles Pooter's, which is square, or old-fashioned.

clue.text: Thief fences small dog

indicators.note: fences means encloses, so the thief word surrounds the small letter

parts.note: a pincher is one who pinches, a thief

explanation.surface: A burglar sells on a little stolen dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fences' looks like a crook selling stolen goods; it means encloses, putting S inside PINCHER.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinscher is a German breed of dog, as in the Doberman pinscher.

clue.text: Oomph in something like rented vehicle

indicators.note: in places the vigour word inside the others

parts.note: CA is short for circa, meaning about or something like
let means rented out
brio is vigour or oomph

explanation.surface: Some get-up-and-go in a hire car.
explanation.walkthrough: CA is circa, Latin for about, hence 'something like'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabriolet is a car with a folding roof, and earlier a light horse-drawn carriage.

clue.text: Hardy and Pinter forged papers

indicators.note: forged means faked or hammered into a new shape, so the playwright's name is reworked

parts.note: ID is identity papers

explanation.surface: Two literary names, Hardy and Pinter, linked to fake documents.
explanation.walkthrough: Hardy looks like Thomas Hardy beside Pinter, but it is the definition. 'forged' rearranges PINTER into INTREP.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardy in the sense of bold and robust; intrepid means fearless.

clue.text: Soldier, number 19

parts.note: the punctuation mark in the clue is a comma
19 is a party or bash, and a do is a party

explanation.surface: A soldier's name and serial number.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed comma gives its own name, COMMA. 'number' is N, and the answer to 19, a bash or party, gives DO.
explanation.definitionFit: A commando is a soldier trained for raids, a member of an elite assault unit.

clue.text: Slug or shot

definitions.meaning: a slug is a heavy blow, so to hit hard
a shot is an attempt, as in to have a go

explanation.definitionFit: A bash is a hard blow, and having a bash at something means having a try.

clue.text: Give old footballer old wife

parts.note: George Best was a famous Northern Irish footballer who played for Manchester United

explanation.surface: Give a veteran footballer his former wife.
explanation.walkthrough: George Best was a famous Manchester United winger of the 1960s.
explanation.definitionFit: To bestow is to give, usually formally, as an honour or gift.

clue.text: One funny way to block ridicule

indicators.note: to block puts the street letters in the middle, blocking the jeering word

parts.note: to jeer is to ridicule
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A funny way to stop people mocking you.
explanation.definitionFit: A jester is a professional fool, a person who is funny for a living.

clue.text: Hill shelters people generally keep

indicators.note: shelters means encloses, so the hill word wraps the people word

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill
we can mean people in general

explanation.surface: Hill shelters where people tend to stay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keep' looks like a verb; it is a castle's stronghold.
explanation.definitionFit: A keep is the main stronghold of a castle, a fortified tower.

clue.text: Vision, certainly in place in blindness

indicators.note: in places the affirmative inside the number

parts.note: the clue for blindness is numbered 8 in this grid, so its place is eight
yes is an emphatic certainly

explanation.surface: Vision, assuredly, is what the blind lack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'place in blindness' means the grid number of that clue, which sits at 8-down.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyesight is the faculty of seeing, one's vision.

clue.text: Language, one that's back to front

indicators.note: to front says the back word is placed at the front of the one

parts.note: hind means at the back, as in hind legs
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A language that reads back to front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back to front' reads as a reversal signal, but here HIND (back) goes to the front of I (one).
explanation.definitionFit: Hindi is a major language of northern India.

clue.text: Contend with what 23 allows

parts.note: to vie is to contend or compete

explanation.surface: A challenge to compete with what sight permits.
explanation.walkthrough: 23 is the answer at 23-across, the faculty of seeing.
explanation.definitionFit: Sight lets you see a scene, which is a view.

clue.text: Blunt end of pencil ____

parts.note: a pencil's sharpened end is its point
the printed gap is a blank

explanation.surface: A blunt pencil, with a missing word to fill in.
explanation.walkthrough: The empty line in the clue is itself a blank.
explanation.definitionFit: Point-blank means direct and frank, so a blunt remark is a point-blank one.

clue.text: Playwright's lowest point — what son rejected

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the pieces are read in reverse

parts.note: the nadir is the lowest point
eh is said for what? when one has not heard

explanation.surface: A playwright's lowest moment, which his son turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: Richard Brinsley Sheridan wrote The Rivals; 'what' is the exclamation of someone who missed what was said.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheridan was an Irish-born playwright, author of The School for Scandal.

clue.text: In 21? Wow!

parts.note: the answer at 21, a funny person, can be called a wit
a hit is a smash success, something that wows

explanation.walkthrough: The 21 is the answer at 21-across, the funny person.
explanation.definitionFit: In means fashionable, and with-it is a dated slang word for trendy.
